title: How to Check Your NPS Balance in 2026: A Practical Guide

faq.a: A PRAN, or Permanent Retirement Account Number, is a unique 12-digit identification number allotted to every NPS subscriber. It is essential for all NPS-related transactions and for accessing your account details online.

faq.q: How often should I check my NPS balance?
faq.a: It's advisable to check your NPS balance quarterly or bi-annually. Daily checks are unnecessary and can lead to anxiety due to market fluctuations, but annual reviews are crucial to ensure your retirement planning is on track.

faq.q: Can I check my NPS balance without a password?
faq.a: No, for security reasons, you generally cannot check your full NPS balance and detailed statement without your password. However, some CRAs might offer a limited view or SMS balance for registered mobile numbers without a full login.

faq.q: What if I forget my PRAN?
faq.a: If you forget your PRAN, you can retrieve it by visiting the CRA portal (NSDL or KFintech) and using the 'Forgot PRAN' option. You will typically need to provide your date of birth, email ID, and the Permanent Account Number (PAN) linked to your NPS account.

faq.q: Are there any charges for checking my NPS balance?
faq.a: No, there are no direct charges for checking your NPS balance through the online CRA portals, mobile apps, or by receiving email statements. Standard SMS charges might apply if you use the SMS service provided by your mobile operator.

faq.q: How do I update my contact details for NPS statements?
faq.a: You can update your email ID, mobile number, and address by logging into your respective CRA portal (NSDL or KFintech) using your PRAN and password. Look for options like 'Update Personal Details' or 'Change Contact Information'.
